Hello, this is Paolo returning your call about the September group. Two things. The first one is good news: the hotel has agreed to hold the ten rooms until the thirtieth, so you have three more weeks than I told you last time. The second thing is less good. The curator who runs the pavilion visits has moved to a Thursday only schedule this season, so if your group arrives on a Friday, we lose that visit completely. If you could move the arrival to a Wednesday, we would fit both the pavilions and the Thursday visit, and honestly it would make the whole week easier. Let me know either way before Friday, because the deposit invoice goes out on Monday and I would rather send you the right one.

Right, a quick briefing before you all go to bed, because tomorrow starts early. Breakfast is from seven, and the boat leaves the dock at ten past eight and will not wait, so please be downstairs at eight. If you are not there, the group goes and you meet us at the pavilion, which is not the end of the world but it costs you the walk. Bring your passport tomorrow and not your card, because the private access list is checked against passports at the door. Marta is our on-site coordinator, she is Italian, she knows everybody in the building, and she is the person to call if anything goes wrong. Not me, and definitely not the office in Milan. And one more thing: the afternoon is free on purpose. Do not fill it. This city punishes people who plan every hour.
